briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Michigan Regulators Keep Swinging the Hammer as National Cannabis Fights Over Repeal, China Ties, and Psychedelics Heat Up
briefs.top: Michigan's Cannabis Regulatory Agency kept up its enforcement streak this week, finalizing a six-figure fine against a Ypsilanti retailer and adding to a run of license revocations stretching back through September, while a state court found a cultivator illegally farmed protected wetlands. Nationally, the fight over Massachusetts' marijuana-repeal ballot measure drew star power and lawmaker pushback, Senate Republicans pressed the DOJ on Chinese-linked illicit grows, and the FDA's psychedelics comment docket closed as the industry awaited its next move.

local.text: CRA revokes Ypsilanti retailer's license, fines it $251,250 — The agency finalized an order against Budbridge LLC, doing business as Muha Meds Ypsilanti, over seven rule violations tied to roughly 900 vape cartridges sold through fake customer profiles built around social media influencers.

Court finds cannabis grower illegally farmed protected wetlands — A Michigan court determined a cultivator destroyed protected wetlands to build out its grow operation, based on an announcement from the state Attorney General's office.

CRA releases disciplinary action and license-denial report — The agency published its latest roundup of disciplinary actions against licensees alongside a new report on denied applications and non-renewed licenses statewide.

$2 million fine, processor license revoked over hidden camera — The CRA closed and revoked Michigan Investment 10 LLC's processor licenses, with Executive Director Brian Hanna noting the facility's extraction-room camera was pointed at a wall instead of the activity it was supposed to monitor.
Hemp processor's license suspended statewide — The CRA immediately suspended Loud Labs of Michigan LLC's hemp processor-handler license, part of the agency's broader late-summer enforcement push.

national.text: GOP senators press DOJ on Chinese-linked illicit grows — Sens. Tom Cotton, Susan Collins, Pete Ricketts and Ted Budd sent Attorney General Todd Blanche a letter demanding a full investigation into Chinese criminal networks' financing, land use and CCP ties in the illicit U.S. cannabis and hemp trade.

Massachusetts lawmakers urge 'No' vote on marijuana repeal — State legislators publicly came out against Question 8, the November ballot measure that would repeal Massachusetts' adult-use cannabis laws, as the campaign heads into its final weeks.

FDA's psychedelics public-comment docket closes — The window to submit comments on the agency's hearing covering future therapeutic use of psilocybin, MDMA and other psychedelics shut on October 5, following a September 14 hearing that drew over 1,800 registered attendees.

Report: missing moisture standards cost states millions — An ATACH-commissioned analysis of nearly 145,000 lab results across 10 states found cannabis flower is routinely over-dried relative to ASTM's recommended water-activity range, stripping terpenes and shrinking the tax base.
Rove enters Canada with Ontario launch — The U.S. vape brand's Diamond Series Minibar is now on shelves through the Ontario Cannabis Store, marking Rove's first market outside the United States.
